answer.text:
On startup Paws runs `recoverOnStartup`, which decides what to do with each unfinished work item in one transaction. Running, verifying, recovering, awaiting-input and merge-queue items are the ones it considers. Its first resumable run is usually a fresh session; a second unfinished start asks in Linear instead of resuming again. Items in the merge queue keep their place, and merges that may have been in flight are checked before they move.

The entry point is `recoverOnStartup` in `src/db/recovery.ts`. It runs inside `immediate(...)`, first shifts runner leases for downtime, then loads items in the states `awaiting_input`, `running`, `verifying`, `recovering` and `merge_queue`, ordered by creation time and id (`src/db/recovery.ts:51-53`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:31-37`) (`src/db/items.ts:148-160`). Paws downtime, up to `offlineBudgetMs`, does not count against an open runner lease (`src/db/recovery.ts:44`).

For each item, the code first checks whether a restart question should be asked, which records an `ask_restart` decision and moves on (`src/db/recovery.ts:58-61`). It then skips items that already have a parked capacity wait, a pending answer resume, or a pending transient retry (`src/db/recovery.ts:62-64`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:103-114`). Otherwise it gathers the runner-holds-work signal, whether a merge call is recorded for the item, and whether a run is active, and passes them to `decideStartup` (`src/db/recovery.ts:65-74`) (`src/db/remote-merges.ts:78-80`).

`decideStartup` in `src/core/recovery.ts` produces the decision, in this order (`src/core/recovery.ts:93-105`):

1. Items outside the resumable set get `none`.
2. A `merge_queue` item with no active run gets `keep_place`, carrying whether a merge call may have been in flight. If a run is active, it gets `reverify` (`src/core/recovery.ts:95-96`).
3. An item whose checkpoint shows a merge in progress gets `reverify` (`src/core/recovery.ts:97`).
4. A `verifying` item whose runner still holds its work gets `reverify`. Any other item whose runner holds work gets `resume` with `reattach` (`src/core/recovery.ts:98-100`).
5. If the item has already been resumed once and that was less than `RESUME_AGAIN_AFTER_MS` ago, it gets `ask_restart` (`src/core/recovery.ts:101-102`). The unit tests show a 45-minute gap resumes again and a 5-minute gap asks (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:92-109`).
6. A `verifying` item with a verification candidate in its checkpoint gets `reverify` with `resumed` set (`src/core/recovery.ts:103-104`).
7. Otherwise it gets `resume` in a fresh session from its checkpoint, or with no checkpoint from its branch (`src/core/recovery.ts:105`) (`src/core/recovery.test.ts:111-120`).

The doc comment on `decideStartup` describes the same rule: a running or verifying item is resumed once in a fresh session, and the next unfinished start asks in Linear whether to start it again (`src/core/recovery.ts:76-78`). A `reverify` cut short by the restart starts over (`src/core/recovery.ts:80-81`).

Applying the result: `resume` decisions get a staggered `runAt`, spaced by `STARTUP_RESUME_SPACING_MS` of 5 seconds (`src/db/recovery.ts:56`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:85`) (`src/db/recovery.ts:39`). A reattached resume or re-verify that is already pending is not applied again (`src/db/recovery.ts:75-86`). After the loop, every `awaiting_input` item with a current run releases its run capacity, and if any such item exists a `startup-questions` catch-up job is enqueued (`src/db/recovery.ts:89-98`).

The README says the same at a high level: runners keep working while Paws is down and keep their results, and Paws reattaches to the same commands after startup, including in-flight Closeout reviews and answer tasks (`README.md:54`). `startLoops` and `startHost` in `src/index.ts` are the other startup pieces, though the evidence only shows their definitions, not how they interact with recovery (`src/db/loops.ts:12-33`) (`src/host/index.ts:10-26`) (`src/index.ts:73-152`).

Test coverage is partial. A stagger test restarts four in-flight items, sets them to `recovering`, calls `recoverOnStartup`, and checks that resume jobs are claimed one at a time as the fake clock advances (`test/startup-resume-stagger.test.ts:143-184`).

This is based on 17 source ranges in 15 files, and research stopped at the deep limit maxPasses, so other relevant code may not have been inspected.
caveats: Research stopped at its pass limit, so several helpers were not read: `ensureRestartQuestion`, `hasPendingAnswerResume`, `hasPendingTransientRetry`, `applyDecision`, `mergeWasInProgress`, `RESUMABLE`, and `runActive`.

The `keep_place` path says the merge job asks GitHub whether an in-flight merge went through [E4:78-80], but the GitHub check code was not in the evidence. Only `mergeCallInFlight` (a row lookup in `merge_call`) was read [E8:78-80].
The exact meaning of `RESUME_AGAIN_AFTER_MS` and the default `offlineBudgetMs` were not in the evidence.
